_comment: Generic architecture contract for governed path placement.
This file owns the SCHEMA and the ROLE VOCABULARY only.
It deliberately contains NO absolute machine paths: the machine instance is
owned by hwz-ops (ops/workspace/environment.yaml#roots) and is supplied by
the caller. Servers, hosts and checkouts differ; roles do not.
See 11-topology-authority-ownership: serveros owns schema, hwz-ops owns instance.

key_note: Two shapes, and which one is live depends on the instance's schema.
v1 (hwz/environment.v1, the Beijing node) carries `roots` directly:
token -> absolute path, in the machine instance.
v2 (hwz/environment.v2, this node) carries NO `roots`. It declares
`binding_authority` and delegates every role root to the device profile
in the serveros repo. A reader that only looks for `roots` therefore
reads a v2 instance as silence -- which is how five bound tokens came
out unresolved on 2026-09-22 while the machine had answered the
question, elsewhere, in a document the reader never opened.
Both shapes are read now; the v2 half is `binding` below.

_comment: How a v2 machine instance delegates. The instance names a profile; the
profile binds paths. The token VOCABULARY stays here (this file owns
the schema and the role vocabulary) and the PATHS stay in the profile,
so the ownership split holds in both directions: nothing absolute is
copied into hwz-ops and no second token table is invented in the reader.
role_to_token names only the roles a profile actually binds. The
workspace children the profile has no role for -- ops, records and
test-envs -- are derived from WORKSPACE_ROOT through
`workspace_root_children` and `roles` above, both already in this file,
rather than repeated as absolutes here.
binding.read_from: the serveros repo, at the canonical ref
_role_to_token_note: WORKSPACE_ROOT is defined as the parent they share, so the parent cannot
be derived until those two are bound.
NOT here: `knowledge.corporate`. The profile's role of that name is the
role is the `knowledge` child of WORKSPACE_ROOT. They are two roles that
happen to share a directory HERE, and mapping them to one token would let
one role's UNBOUND delete a structural position the contract states in
its own right -- which is how a role vocabulary quietly loses a member.

workspace_parent.rule: the common parent of the two roles. If they disagree the token stays unresolved rather than guessed, because taking either one alone would accept a profile whose src/ and worktrees/ are not siblings -- and this contract describes a layout in which they are.

roots_source.note: Machine instance. Never duplicated here. If this file grew absolute paths, the ownership split would be violated.
_derivations_note: RELATIVE derivations, not paths. They express 'this root is <this parent>
plus this segment' -- the absolute value still comes from the machine
instance, so nothing is duplicated and the ownership split holds.
Why this block exists (2026-09-11): the 14 roles below name 14 root tokens,
but the machine instance declares only 9 keys (DATA_ROOT, WORKSPACE_ROOT,
DATA_PLANE_ROOT, LOCAL_DATA_ROOT). The remaining tokens -- ARTIFACTS_ROOT,
TOOLCHAINS_ROOT, WORKTREES_ROOT, STATE_ROOT and the four DATA_ROOT/<x>
sub-roots -- had NO machine-readable definition anywhere. Every consumer
therefore re-derived them by concatenating strings, each in its own way,
which is exactly how a 'role' drifts from a path without anyone editing
the contract. STATE_ROOT additionally duplicates state_root.rule below;
the resolver reads state_root.rule first and this entry is the fallback.
A role whose token is in neither the machine instance nor this block is

_run_pattern_note: DERIVED FROM THE MACHINE, not invented. Every Run directory under
ARTIFACTS_ROOT/skills/ was read: 24 of 25 are RUN-<yyyymmdd>-<slug>
The previous value was '^RUN-[0-9]{4,}$'. On this machine it matched
exactly one directory -- the legacy outlier sitting at the CANCELLED
skills/<skill>/<project>/<RUN> level -- and rejected all 24 real ones.
A declared pattern that describes the accident and not the practice is
worse than no pattern: a resolver following it would have refused every
Both shapes are accepted so that a read of an existing Run is never
denied. New Runs use the date-slug form.
naming.note: Lexical rules for path segments. Declared here so the resolver and the artifact_workdir helper cannot drift apart on what a legal segment is.

state_root.note: Ability/Skill state namespaces live UNDER state/serveros/<namespace>, never at state/<namespace>. The srv-0003 C1 correction.

run-output.note: A run WITH an Item. project/ITEM/RUN are all path levels.

note: A Skill run with NO Item: skills/<skill>/<RUN>, two levels.
project is run metadata/scope, NOT a directory level. The previous
template skills/<skill>/<project>/<RUN> was cancelled because it
inserted a project directory the machine's actual runs do not have.
The 17 existing runs already match the corrected layout; nothing is
migrated, because nothing was wrong on disk -- the template was.
Machine-emitted operational output (e.g. logs/litellm). It was on disk
and undeclared until 2026-09-11, so every consumer that wanted it built
the path itself. Distinct from dynamic-state: state/ is control-plane
state that is READ; logs/ is output that is only ever appended.
Software that no package manager owns (apps/ + cli/). Distinct from
toolchain: a toolchain is version-managed per language (nvm/gopath/npm);
software/ is the root for standalone binaries that have no such manager.
environment.yaml records it as present-and-empty by design -- a reserved
root, declared here so its emptiness is a fact rather than a surprise.
Regenerable scratch space. Nothing durable may live here; a consumer
that finds a durable artefact under tmp/ has found a placement bug.

data_root_children_note: The previous list had 8 entries against 12 directories on disk. §10 says a
stable root is not deleted for being rare, so the CONTRACT gained
logs/ software/ tmp/ rather than the machine losing them.
checked by UNREGISTERED_DATA_ROOT in architecture_check.py. Before that the
block was decorative: nothing read it, so nothing could notice it was wrong.
.vscode-server    platform-owned (VS Code remote server), not a ServerOS
root; excluded by the leading-dot rule in the checker
workspace         IS the WORKSPACE_ROOT -- a declared root, not a child of
one; it appears under DATA_ROOT physically and is
skipped by name in the checker

_comment: C2: record requirements are driven by the record's SEMANTIC ROLE, not by the
records root. A flat records.requires=[project,item] would wrongly reject
records/managed-documents/. This map is illustrative and open-ended: the
resolution rule is 'look up the role', not 'enumerate every record type'.

forbidden_patterns.note: Substitute roots that shadow DATA_ROOT buckets.

forbidden_patterns.match: workspace/<child> where child not in workspace_root_children
forbidden_patterns.note: NO NEW DEBT. Additions are rejected before creation; existing legacy paths are LEGACY_COMPAT, never retro-DENY.

forbidden_patterns.match: state/<namespace> where namespace not in {serveros, personal}
forbidden_patterns.note: state/ is a DATA_ROOT root whose ServerOS-owned child is state/serveros. state/<ns> is the pre-C1 shape.
